answer: If you feel your husband is running the marriage, the only sustainable choice is to file for a quick no-fault divorce. Courts in every state essentially require 12 months of separation if you live in a traditional divorce state or a year of separation in newer quick-departure states like California because they used to be common options. Legal separation is typically cheaper and quicker than full divorce in most places, so you can usually petition for one first and then pursue divorce afterward if you haven’t yet achieved peace. Avoid asking a therapist initially because therapy can prolong the healing process; instead, seek attorneys for guidance during the court process.
